reference: GNU coreutils rmdir(1) from the runner's reference PATH, with GNU mkdir and ln used only to create private fixtures. Each parity script runs unchanged under system Bash and bash-os with candidate PATH empty; failures are captured where effects must still be inspected. The metadata contract uses the pinned stock Bash rmdir documentation and builtin type metadata.
coverage: Remove one empty directory and verify the tree is empty.
Remove nested directories with separate child-then-parent operands.
GNU -p parent removal, including partial removal and final error status.
Handle a spaced path and a dash-prefixed basename through a ./ path.
Accept a trailing slash on an empty directory operand.
Reject a nonempty directory and preserve its contents.
Report a missing operand path and retain the expected filesystem state.
Continue across operands after a nonempty-directory error and remove a later empty directory.
Reject a symlink to a directory without removing either link or target.
Compare the no-operand error status and verify builtin/help registration.
exclusions: Permission-denied and read-only-filesystem cases are omitted because this fixture does not set up independent privilege or mount conditions.
Exact diagnostic wording is not asserted; stderr presence or absence and resulting tree are checked.
GNU-only options beyond -p, such as --verbose and --ignore-fail-on-non-empty, are not covered.
No host, device, network, privileged, stress, or destructive system operations are involved.

cases.purpose: Remove one empty relative directory and verify successful status, no output, and removal.
cases.script: mkdir target; rmdir target; [[ ! -e target ]]; printf 'removed\n'

cases.purpose: Remove an empty child and then its parent as two ordered operands.
cases.script: mkdir top; mkdir top/inner; rmdir top/inner top; [[ ! -e top ]]; printf 'removed\n'

cases.purpose: Check GNU rmdir -p semantics, capturing command status so the parent-removal effect is compared even if the candidate rejects the option.
cases.script: mkdir chain; mkdir chain/leaf; set +e; rmdir -p chain/leaf; rc=$?; set -e; if [[ -e chain ]]; then parent=retained; else parent=removed; fi; printf 'status=%s parent=%s\n' "$rc" "$parent"

cases.purpose: Remove a path containing spaces and a dash-prefixed directory addressed through ./.
cases.script: mkdir 'two words'; mkdir ./-odd; rmdir 'two words' ./-odd; [[ ! -e 'two words' && ! -e ./-odd ]]; printf 'removed 2\n'

cases.purpose: Accept a trailing slash on an empty directory operand.
cases.script: mkdir trailing; rmdir trailing/; [[ ! -e trailing ]]; printf 'removed\n'

cases.purpose: Return failure for a nonempty directory while preserving the directory and its file.
cases.script: mkdir nonempty; printf 'payload\n' > nonempty/file; set +e; rmdir nonempty; rc=$?; set -e; if [[ -e nonempty/file ]]; then state=retained; else state=missing; fi; printf 'status=%s file=%s\n' "$rc" "$state"

cases.purpose: Report a nonexistent directory operand, capture its status, and leave the fixture tree unchanged.
cases.script: set +e; rmdir missing; rc=$?; set -e; printf 'status=%s\n' "$rc"

cases.purpose: Verify that a nonempty first operand does not prevent removal of a later empty operand; also include a missing operand in the aggregate failure.
cases.script: mkdir blocked; printf 'keep\n' > blocked/file; mkdir later; set +e; rmdir blocked later absent; rc=$?; set -e; if [[ -e blocked/file ]]; then blocked_state=retained; else blocked_state=missing; fi; if [[ -e later ]]; then later_state=retained; else later_state=removed; fi; printf 'status=%s blocked=%s later=%s\n' "$rc" "$blocked_state" "$later_state"

cases.purpose: Reject a symlink operand and leave both the symlink and its empty target directory intact.
cases.script: mkdir target; ln -s target link; set +e; rmdir link; rc=$?; set -e; if [[ -L link && -d target ]]; then state=retained; else state=changed; fi; printf 'status=%s state=%s\n' "$rc" "$state"

cases.purpose: Compare the utility-level failure status for a no-operand invocation while capturing it to keep the fixture script successful.
Assert Bash reports rmdir as a builtin and that its documented help entry exists, without treating metadata as operation coverage.
The -- terminator allows a dash-leading directory.
Parent removal handles repeated and trailing separators.
Parent removal stops with failure at a nonempty ancestor, retaining its other contents.
cases.script: mkdir -p tree/a/b; printf keep > tree/retained; rmdir -p tree/a/b

cases.purpose: An explicit dot ancestor is attempted and diagnosed after its empty children are removed.
